anchor.exact: On Sakhalin, three genealogically different languages, Ainu (language isolate), Nivkh (language isolate), and Uilta (Tungusic) came into contact through social and economic activities.

statement.en: On the island of Sakhalin, three genealogically distinct languages—Ainu, Nivkh, and Uilta—came into contact through social and economic activities.
statement.ja: サハリン島において、系統を異にする3言語であるアイヌ語、ニヴフ語、ウィルタ語が社会・経済活動を通じて接触した。

entailment.quote: On Sakhalin, three genealogically different languages, Ainu (language isolate), Nivkh (language isolate), and Uilta (Tungusic) came into contact through social and economic activities.

anchor.exact: a number of linguistic characteristics not found in the dialects of other regions or in sister languages can be found in which they resemble each other (Kindaichi 1944; Yamada 2008, 2010; Kazama 2009; Pevnov 2009; Gusev 2015, and others)

statement.en: Ainu, Nivkh, and Uilta share a number of linguistic characteristics that are not found in the dialects of other regions or in their respective sister languages.
statement.ja: アイヌ語、ニヴフ語、ウィルタ語の間には、他地域の諸方言や同系統の言語には見られない共通の言語的特徴が複数存在する。

entailment.quote: a number of linguistic characteristics not found in the dialects of other regions or in sister languages can be found in which they resemble each other

anchor.exact: some settlements which had names in two languages, e.g., Poro kotan and Pile vo, meaning ‘big settlement’ in Ainu and Nivkh, respectively

statement.en: Some settlements on Sakhalin had names in both Ainu and Nivkh, such as Ainu Poro kotan and Nivkh Pile vo, both meaning 'big settlement'.
statement.ja: サハリンの集落にはアイヌ語の Poro kotan とニヴフ語の Pile vo（いずれも「大集落」の意）のように、2言語で並行する地名をもつものがあった。

entailment.quote: as exemplified by some settlements which had names in two languages, e.g., Poro kotan and Pile vo, meaning ‘big settlement’ in Ainu and Nivkh, respectively.

anchor.exact: Linguistically speaking, among the dialects of Ainu, it is the Sakhalin dialect which mostly exhibits characteristics common to Nivkh and Uilta (Kindaichi 1944

statement.en: Among the dialects of Ainu, it is the Sakhalin dialect that exhibits the most characteristics in common with Nivkh and Uilta.
statement.ja: アイヌ語の諸方言のなかで、ニヴフ語やウィルタ語と共通する特徴を最も多く示すのは樺太方言である。

entailment.quote: among the dialects of Ainu, it is the Sakhalin dialect which mostly exhibits characteristics common to Nivkh and Uilta

anchor.exact: Ikegami (2004: 222) states, “Of the Ainu words that were borrowed into other languages of Karafuto [Sakhalin], not many were transmitted to the continent.”

statement.en: Ainu loanwords borrowed into other languages of Sakhalin were very rarely transmitted to the Asian continent.
statement.ja: サハリンの他の言語に借用されたアイヌ語の単語のうち、大陸に伝わったものはきわめて少ない。

entailment.quote: Of the Ainu words that were borrowed into other languages of Karafuto [Sakhalin], not many were transmitted to the continent.

anchor.exact: there is no record of Ainu being spoken on the continent.

statement.en: There is no historical record of the Ainu language ever having been spoken on the Asian continent.
statement.ja: アイヌ語が大陸で話されていたという記録は存在しない。

entailment.quote: there is no record of Ainu being spoken on the continent.

anchor.exact: some are derived from Ainu (e.g. -kur, meaning ‘people’ in Ainu).

statement.en: Nineteenth-century Japanese records preserve names of ethnic groups derived from the Ainu element -kur, meaning 'people'.
statement.ja: 19世紀の日本語記録には、「人」を意味するアイヌ語要素 -kur に由来する民族名が現れる。

entailment.quote: some are derived from Ainu (e.g. -kur, meaning ‘people’ in Ainu).

anchor.exact: an Ainu word used by Toyottono (recorded by Matsuda) sinjitsu ‘origin’ is closer to the Taraika dialect sincit [ʃinʤit] ‘root’ than to the sinris of the Raichiska dialect found on west coast

statement.en: The Ainu word sinjitsu 'origin' recorded from a Sirunkur speaker is cognate with and phonologically closer to Taraika dialect sincit [ʃinʤit] 'root' than to Raichiska dialect sinris on the west coast.
statement.ja: シルンクル話者から記録されたアイヌ語単語 sinjitsu（起源）は、西海岸のライチシカ方言の sinris よりも、東海岸タライカ方言の sincit [ʃinʤit]（根）に近い。

entailment.quote: an Ainu word used by Toyottono ... sinjitsu ‘origin’ is closer to the Taraika dialect sincit ... than to the sinris of the Raichiska dialect

anchor.exact: In contrast, the number of lexical borrowings in common with Ainu is comparatively small, suggesting that language contact along the north-south axis of the island of Sakhalin was local and limited.

statement.en: In Nivkh, lexical borrowings in common with Ainu are comparatively few, suggesting that language contact along the north-south axis of Sakhalin was local and limited.
statement.ja: ニヴフ語においてアイヌ語と共通する借用語は比較的少なく、樺太の南北軸に沿った言語接触が局所的かつ限定的であったことを示唆している。

entailment.quote: the number of lexical borrowings in common with Ainu is comparatively small, suggesting that language contact along the north-south axis of the island of Sakhalin was local and limited.

anchor.exact: The fact that, of the dialects of Nivkh, the Poronaisk dialect stands out in exceptionally having a large number of loans in common with Ainu, supports the local nature of contact between the two languages.

statement.en: The Poronaisk dialect of Nivkh exceptionally has a large number of loanwords in common with Ainu compared to other Nivkh dialects, supporting the localized nature of contact between the two languages.
statement.ja: ニヴフ語の方言の中でポロナイスク方言は例外的にアイヌ語と共通の借用語を多く有しており、両言語間の接触の局所性を裏付けている。

entailment.quote: of the dialects of Nivkh, the Poronaisk dialect stands out in exceptionally having a large number of loans in common with Ainu, supports the local nature of contact between the two languages.

anchor.exact: There is a possibility that, including the contact situation on the west coast (Sirunkur), about which there is almost no record, the central region of Sakhalin, where the Ainu came into contact with the Nivkh and the Uilta, developed a unique language use situation

statement.en: The central region of Sakhalin, where the Ainu contacted the Nivkh and Uilta, may have developed a unique language use situation distinct from other regions of the island.
statement.ja: アイヌがニヴフやウイルタと接触した樺太中央部は、他の地域とは異なる独特の言語使用状況を発達させた可能性がある。

entailment.quote: There is a possibility that... the central region of Sakhalin, where the Ainu came into contact with the Nivkh and the Uilta, developed a unique language use situation different from that of other regions.

anchor.exact: Loan words common to Ainu, Nivkh, and Uilta (31 words)

statement.en: Thirty-one loanwords are identified as common across Ainu, Nivkh, and Uilta on Sakhalin.
statement.ja: 樺太においてアイヌ語、ニヴフ語、ウイルタ語に共通する借用語として31語が同定される。

entailment.quote: Loan words common to Ainu, Nivkh, and Uilta (31 words)

entailment.quote: Loan words common to Nivkh and Ainu (29 words)

entailment.quote: Loan words common to Ainu and Uilta (13 words)

anchor.exact: As for Ainu, the Hokkaido dialects have the loan sato (HA), but in the dialects of Sakhalin only otoopenpe (SA) with the broader meaning of ‘something sweet’ is found.

statement.en: In Hokkaido Ainu, the Japanese loan sato is used for 'sugar', whereas in Sakhalin dialects only otoopenpe 'something sweet' is found.
statement.ja: 北海道アイヌ語では「砂糖」を表すのに日本語からの借用語satoが用いられるが、樺太方言ではより広い「甘いもの」を意味するotoopenpeのみが見られる。

entailment.quote: Ainu, the Hokkaido dialects have the loan sato (HA), but in the dialects of Sakhalin only otoopenpe (SA) with the broader meaning of 'something sweet' is found.
entailment.note: The passage says 'Hokkaido dialects' not necessarily all Hokkaido Ainu, and 'only otoopenpe' is stated for Sakhalin, matching the scope as 'all'.

anchor.exact: Ainu used a loan word from Japanese, such as konkaani (SA).

statement.en: Sakhalin Ainu konkaani 'metal, gold' is a loanword from Japanese.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語のkonkaani（金属、金）は日本語からの借用語である。

entailment.quote: Ainu used a loan word from Japanese, such as konkaani (SA).

anchor.exact: On the other hand, hasami (SA, HA) is clearly a loan word from Japanese.

statement.en: Ainu hasami 'scissors' in both Sakhalin and Hokkaido dialects is a loanword from Japanese.
statement.ja: 樺太および北海道アイヌ語のhasami（鋏）は明らかに日本語からの借用語である。

entailment.quote: hasami (SA, HA) is clearly a loan word from Japanese.

anchor.exact: Chiri (1973a: 448, 1973b: 51) holds that nuso (SA) is a borrowing from Nivkh nuci. Certainly, in the Poronaisk dialect of Nivkh there is the word nuci referring to the dog sled as a whole (Tangiku 2013b: 130) and it would be consistent to think that nuso/nuhsu (SA) is a borrowing from that.

statement.en: Sakhalin Ainu nuso or nuhsu 'dog sled' is a borrowing from Nivkh nuci.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語のnuso / nuhsu（犬ぞり一式）はニヴフ語nuciからの借用である。

entailment.quote: Chiri (1973a: 448, 1973b: 51) holds that nuso (SA) is a borrowing from Nivkh nuci.

statement.en: Nivkh [t] corresponds to Sakhalin Ainu [r] in loanwords between the two languages, as in Nivkh maxt to Sakhalin Ainu mahru 'towline spreader' and Nivkh mut to Sakhalin Ainu muhru 'pillow'.

entailment.quote: panco is held to be borrowed from Japanese banshō ‘carpenter’ (Kubodera 1992: 200).

anchor.exact: On the other hand, kaya (SA, HA) is used to refer to both fish skin clothing and sails.

statement.en: Ainu kaya refers to both fish-skin clothing and sails in Sakhalin and Hokkaido, though in Hokkaido dialects the 'fish-skin' sense has bleached and it refers simply to sails.
statement.ja: アイヌ語のkayaは樺太および北海道において魚皮衣と帆の双方を指すが、北海道方言では「魚皮」の意味が脱落して単に「帆」を指す単語になっている。

entailment.quote: kaya (SA, HA) is used to refer to both fish skin clothing and sails.
entailment.note: The passage does not mention the bleaching of the fish-skin sense in Hokkaido.

anchor.exact: Japanese todo ‘sea lion’ is thought to be a borrowing from (25) tonto (HA) ‘hairless thick hide, tanned leather’ (Kindaichi 1993).

statement.ja: 日本語のトド（海驢）は、北海道アイヌ語のtonto（無毛の厚皮、なめし革）からの借用と考えられている。

entailment.quote: Japanese todo ‘sea lion’ is thought to be a borrowing from (25) tonto (HA) ‘hairless thick hide, tanned leather’ (Kindaichi 1993).

statement.ja: 北海道アイヌ語では、毛のない動物標本はすべてtontone（tontoのようである）と呼ばれた。

entailment.quote: Not only sea-lions but any hairless animal specimen was called tontone ‘like a tonto’ (S. Tamura 1996).

entailment.quote: Ikegami (1994) hypothesizes that san (SA, HA) ‘shelf for offerings’ has the same source.

entailment.quote: ontaro (HA) and ontoro (SA), both borrowings from the Japanese taru ‘barrel, cask’

anchor.exact: In addition, the shallow (45) ‘birch bark plate’ found in Nivkh haŋr̥ (SN) has entered Sakhalin Ainu as hankata. Since the word-final -r̥ can be analyzed as a nominal ending in Nivkh, it can be hypothesized that the borrowing was from Nivkh to Ainu.

statement.en: Sakhalin Ainu hankata 'birch bark plate' was borrowed from Nivkh haŋr̥.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語のhankata（白樺樹皮皿）はニヴフ語haŋr̥からの借用である。

entailment.quote: has entered Sakhalin Ainu as hankata... it can be hypothesized that the borrowing was from Nivkh to Ainu

anchor.exact: Looking solely at the form of the words, it is possible that Nivkh borrowed the word from Ainu. The accent on nikar (SA) is on the second syllable and an unaccented initial vowel is easily lost in Nivkh (ɲŋar̥).

statement.en: Nivkh ɲŋar̥ 'ladder' was possibly borrowed from Sakhalin Ainu nikar, where the loss of the unaccented first syllable reflects the second-syllable accent of nikar.
statement.ja: ニヴフ語ɲŋar̥（梯子）は樺太アイヌ語nikarからの借用の可能性があり、nikarが第2音節にアクセントをもつため無アクセントの語頭母音が脱落したと考えられる。

entailment.quote: it is possible that Nivkh borrowed the word from Ainu. The accent on nikar (SA) is on the second syllable and an unaccented initial vowel is easily lost in Nivkh (ɲŋar̥)

anchor.exact: The names vary, but, as has long been pointed out, tɨŋrɨŋ (SN, AN) and tonkori (SA) are thought to be loans from Manchu (Ikegami 1988).

statement.en: Sakhalin Ainu tonkori 'stringed musical instrument' is thought to be a loan from Manchu.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語のtonkori（弦楽器）は満洲語からの借用語であると考えられている。

entailment.quote: tonkori (SA) are thought to be loans from Manchu (Ikegami 1988)

anchor.exact: Within Sakhalin Ainu, this word is only used on the west coast of Sakhalin; on the east coast another word, matumere, is used.

statement.en: On the west coast of Sakhalin, Ainu uses the Uilta loanword wampakka for 'mittens', whereas on the east coast the word matumere is used.
statement.ja: 樺太西海岸のアイヌ語では「ミトン」にウイルタ語からの借用語wampakkaが用いられるのに対し、東海岸ではmatumereという語が用いられる。

entailment.quote: Within Sakhalin Ainu, this word is only used on the west coast of Sakhalin; on the east coast another word, matumere, is used. The most likely possibility is that the west coast Sakhalin Ainu borrowed this word completely from [Uilta]
